results.algorithmDescription: MAP is an unsupervised clustering algorithm that uses counts of ICD codes and Concept Unique Identifier (CUI) mentions along with healthcare utilization as measured by total number of ICD codes to predict the phenotype. The output of MAP includes the probability of having the disease for each patient as well as a threshold value that can be used to classify the binary disease status. Those with probability higher than the threshold is considered as a case for the phenotype. See here for detailed description of the MAP algorithm.  There are 1866 MAP phenotypes, each corresponding a Phecode from J. Denny's "Phecode Map" (Denny et al, 1) containing both ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes.   Each patient is assigned a probability from 0 to 1 of having Skin cancer. The probability cutoff denotes the point over which a patient should be labeled as having the condition. For this phenotype, the cutoff of 0.35 means that patients with a MAP probability over 0.35 should be categorized as having Skin cancer.

results.fullName: Primary Malignancy, Other Skin and Subcutaneous Tissue (HDR UK)
results.algorithmDescription:
At the specified date, a patient is defined as having had Primary Malignancy Skin IF they meet the criteria for any of the following on or before the specified date. The earliest date on which the individual meets any of the following criteria on or before the specified date is defined as the first event date:


Primary care


1. Primary Malignancy Skin diagnosis or history of diagnosis during a consultation 

OR
Secondary care


1. ALL diagnoses of Primary Malignancy Skin or history of diagnosis during a hospitalization
